 ## PIMS versions
 
-- Each external event is published three times, as PIMS v0.1.0, v0.2.0 and v0.3.0, so PIMS can move to a newer version when it is ready. The v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 copies' ASB `MessageId` is the same id with `-v2` or `-v3` appended. All three go to the same session, in that order.
-- v0.1.0 is published first. A v0.2.0 or v0.3.0 mapping or publish failure is logged with the schema version, counted as failed (the `notification.message` meter in [observability.md](observability.md#other-metrics)) and never fails or retries the SQS message, because a redelivery would send v0.1.0 a second time. One failing does not stop the other.
+- Each external event is published four times, as PIMS v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0 and v0.4.0, so PIMS can move to a newer version when it is ready. The v0.2.0, v0.3.0 and v0.4.0 copies' ASB `MessageId` is the same id with `-v2`, `-v3` or `-v4` appended. All four go to the same session, in that order.
+- v0.1.0 is published first. A v0.2.0, v0.3.0 or v0.4.0 mapping or publish failure is logged with the schema version, counted as failed (the `notification.message` meter in [observability.md](observability.md#other-metrics)) and never fails or retries the SQS message, because a redelivery would send v0.1.0 a second time. One failing does not stop the other.
 - Each version stamps its own `schemaVersion` and `schemaUri` instead of passing on the incoming event's values. PIMS tells the streams apart by these values.
-- Each version has its own records (`pims/gbnag`, `pims/gbnagv2`, `pims/gbnagv3`), event (`PimsEventV1`, `PimsEventV2`, `PimsEventV3`) and mappers (`Pims*Mapper`, `Pims*MapperV2`, `Pims*MapperV3`), even where a newer version only adds fields to an older one. A change for one version never touches another, and when PIMS has moved off a version, that version is retired by deleting its package, its mappers, its `PimsPayloadMapper` method and its line in `NotificationSqsListener`. These copies are deliberate, so `sonar.cpd.exclusions` in `pom.xml` leaves the per-version records, events and mappers out of SonarCloud's duplication check. Every other SonarCloud rule still applies to them.
-- The envelope records (actor, status change, metadata) are the same in every version, so `PimsEnvelopeMapper` maps them once. `PimsCommonMapperV2` and `PimsCommonMapperV3` do the same for the records that several mappers of their version share. Neither has dependencies, so every mapper can inject them without a bean cycle. `PimsMapperSupport` holds static helpers with no domain meaning.

A change for one of them never touches another. These copies are deliberate, so `sonar.cpd.exclusions` in `pom.xml` leaves the per-version records, events and mappers out of SonarCloud's duplication check. Every other SonarCloud rule still applies to them.
+- v0.4.0 differs from v0.3.0 only in that its exchanged document has no `issuer`, so it has its own event (`PimsEventV4`), `PimsEventMapperV4`, `PimsGbnAgDataMapperV4` and `pims/gbnagv4`, which holds only `PimsExchangedDocument` and `PimsGbnAgData`. Every other v0.4.0 record and mapping rule is the v0.3.0 one (`pims/gbnagv3`, `PimsConsignmentMapperV3`, `PimsCommonMapperV3`), so a change to one of those rules changes both versions. When PIMS has moved off a version, that version is retired by deleting its event, its mappers, its `PimsPayloadMapper` method and its line in `NotificationSqsListener`, and its records unless a later version uses them.
+- The envelope records (actor, status change, metadata) are the same in every version, so `PimsEnvelopeMapper` maps them once. `PimsCommonMapperV2` and `PimsCommonMapperV3` do the same for the records that several mappers of their version share, and v0.4.0 uses `PimsCommonMapperV3`. Neither has dependencies, so every mapper can inject them without a bean cycle. `PimsMapperSupport` holds static helpers with no domain meaning.
 
 ## Fields
 
 - The v0.1.0 records leave out every field the backend outbox never fills. `finalDestinationLocation` is left out because the v0.1.0 schema has no such field.
 - In v0.1.0, `applicableClassification` on a trade line item is a single object: the backend sends exactly one, and the mapper takes the first.
-- In v0.2.0 and v0.3.0, a trade line item has no `typeCode` or `urlId`: they are resolved downstream from CN-code reference data. In v0.2.0 an exchanged document has no `issuer`, a referenced document carries only type code, identifier and issue date, and the origin country has no `regionOfOriginCode`. v0.3.0 adds all three: the issuer is the consignment contact, the referenced document's `urlId` names the document-type list, and the region of origin code is passed through. See `schemas/profiles/imports/gb/pims/gbn-ag-pims-v0.2.0-changes.md` and `gbn-ag-pims-v0.3.0-changes.md` in `trade-imports-schemas`.
+- In v0.2.0 and v0.3.0, a trade line item has no `typeCode` or `urlId`: they are resolved downstream from CN-code reference data. In v0.2.0 an exchanged document has no `issuer`, a referenced document carries only type code, identifier and issue date, and the origin country has no `regionOfOriginCode`. v0.3.0 adds the referenced document's `urlId`, which names the document-type list, and passes the region of origin code through. No message the gateway sends carries an `issuer`: v0.3.0 messages leave it out and the v0.4.0 schema drops it. See `schemas/profiles/imports/gb/pims/gbn-ag-pims-v0.2.0-changes.md`, `gbn-ag-pims-v0.3.0-changes.md` and `gbn-ag-pims-v0.4.0-changes.md` in `trade-imports-schemas`.
+- A backend released before the issuer was removed still sends `exchangedDocument.issuer`. The gateway accepts it and sends it in no stream, so the gateway and the backend can deploy in either order. Every other unknown property still fails the message as non-retryable.
+- The origin country's subdivision is the one with UNCL3227 location function `106`, which the code list calls "Region of origin": the country subdivision the goods came from. It is not the region of origin code, which is a disease zone.
 - Where the schema requires a list to have at least one item (`minItems: 1`), the record component uses `@JsonInclude(NON_EMPTY)`, so an empty list is left out rather than sent as `[]`. Mappers always return an empty list, never null.
